observed: Long irregular ridge-top compound, pale stone curtains and open grounds; no single rectangular generic castle plan.
Western compound combines a tall roofless round tower, a flat-sided polygonal tower with a dark flat cap, a broad cylindrical interior keep and low corner bastions.

Surviving royal lodgings have tall gables and roofs visible in the first photograph. The second panorama shows roofless lodging gables; use the first photograph for the roof treatment and record this difference rather than copying the older-looking roofless state.
A separate tall square clock/entrance tower terminates the eastern part of the long curtain. Trees hide portions of walls and courtyard subdivisions, so PMTiles should supply the component plans.
currentRoundInspection.limits: Exterior pictures only; mapped components control approximate scale and plan. No surveyed dimensions, buried eastern archaeological reconstruction or historical chronology. Photographs linked only.
